End-to-end demo, recorded from a real headless TUI run of this branch (driven by opencode-drive with a simulated model; file writes and hot reload are real):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/242bd982-b293-49da-851b-d62db6f9845c

What it shows, in order:

1. The agent creates `.opencode/plugins/tui/clock.tsx` mid-conversation and a live ticking clock appears above the composer (the new `session.composer.top` slot) with no restart.
2. A second edit swaps the running plugin in place: date added, accent color cycling per second.
3. A save with a syntax error triggers the failure toast while the previous version keeps ticking (keep-last-good).
4. The fix swaps in a live seconds progress bar.

One harness note: the drive sandbox isolates the simulated project from the checkout's node_modules, so the fixture includes a `solid-js` shim pointing at the host instance. A normal project needs no shim; the runtime import rewrite covers it (that's the setup the earlier demo video in the PR body used).

Problem B maps closely to a boundary we've been working on in [GoodMemory](https://github.com/hjqcan/GoodMemory) (I'm the maintainer): durable, inspectable cross-session memory for coding agents through MCP.

OpenCode already works with it through a local MCP block; the version-pinned OpenCode setup is here: https://github.com/hjqcan/GoodMemory/blob/v0.7.2/docs/GoodMemory-OpenCode-Setup-Guide.md

Quick start:

```bash
npm install -g goodmemory@0.7.2
```

Then add the documented `mcp.goodmemory` block to `opencode.json` and verify with `goodmemory_stats`. Writes are opt-in; the default surface is read-only. Node.js 20+ and Bun 1.3.14+ are required by the current launcher.

This would not solve Problem A's native hypothesis-loop detection, nor the proposed file-mtime cache. Those still belong in OpenCode. It can, however, preserve goals, decisions, corrections, and debugging hypotheses across sessions so the next session does not start from zero.

Disclosure: this is a maintainer-provided workaround, not independent adoption evidence.

Root-caused this on my end — not an opencode core bug. It was one of my own local plugins (`~/.config/opencode/plugins/javagt-workflow-guardrails.js`) throwing `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'event.system.push')` inside the `"request"` session hook. That plugin assumed `event.system` was always an array; when it was `undefined`, the uncaught exception killed `SessionRunner.drain` for the session entirely (confirmed via server logs — "Failed to drain Session"). Since the code that clears the plugin's pending-message queue never ran (the throw happens before it), every subsequent turn hit the same crash, which matches the "follow-up message unsticks the UI but produces no output" symptom exactly.

I've removed the plugin locally and the issue is resolved for me. Closing this one out — it's not a core defect, just an unguarded third-party plugin hook. Sorry for the noise, and thanks for the pointer to the related issues.

Addressed by #39748. Automatic title attempts now coalesce only while in flight rather than latching permanently, later successful executions can retry after an initial failure, and title generation reads the first user message even after later prompts arrive. Durable checks and a sequence-guarded rename ensure explicit/manual titles win, including races during generation. Focused runner and title regressions cover failure followed by recovery. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #39747, with retry behavior completed in #39748. V2 session storage, schema, protocol, and generated clients now represent untitled sessions with an absent title; newly created and forked sessions persist `NULL`, while App, TUI, CLI/ACP, export, search, subagent, and sharing surfaces derive display fallbacks at their boundaries. The migration preserves existing rows, and generated/manual titles remain durable and protected from overwrite. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Closing this. On further investigation the empty responses come from network-level flakiness between client and server (connections reset/aborted mid-response during a network flap), not from the opencode server itself — it returns the full list reliably on a healthy connection. The actual bug was client-side: my JSON parser silently treated an empty/truncated 200 body as a successful empty result and overwrote a good cached list; that's now fixed in the client (treat a simultaneous empty from both endpoints as suspicious, keep the last good list, retry). Withdrawing since this isn't a server issue. Sorry for the noise.
